name: Cargomatic — admin, carrier, shipper & driver
description: Every portal, end to end. Admin: order booking and the shorthaul wizard, leg management, accessorials, billing, invoicing, payouts, EDI, documents, audit and Unified View. Carrier: pending tasks, shipment actions, complete stop and POD, offers, payments, drivers. Shipper: booking, invoices, accessorial approval. Plus the driver record. Every node carries the selector the Playwright suite uses; every mutating node carries the API call it fires and the GET that confirms it landed.

env.apiPrefixNote: The admin client calls bare /api/... and /admin/api/... . The edge gateway (proxymatic-edge-*) serves them under /mono, so a browser-observed URL is apiPrefix + path. Match on the suffix, not the whole URL.

sources.note: Every node.selector is copied from a page-object constant named in node.source. Changing a selector here does not change the suite — fix the page object and re-sync.
Express route registrations (app.<method>('<path>')). Path params are the monolith's own (:orderId, :jobId).

kind.section: A region of a page that groups fields and actions.
kind.modal: A dialog. Children are only reachable while it is open.
kind.field: An input the test writes to.

legend.api.await: The request the action fires. The step is not done until this settles.
legend.api.verify: The read-back that proves it persisted. scope=record re-reads the whole entity; scope=field re-reads one field; scope=collection re-reads the list.
legend.api.capture: JSON Pointers lifted out of the await/verify response into flow variables, referenced elsewhere as {name}.
legend.api.verifyNotApplicable: Why this write has no read-back. Set it only when none exists — it removes the node from the gap count.
legend.attachesTo: This node lives in another chunk's UI (its menu, its page) but belongs to this chunk's story. Open that chunk to see it in context.
legend.api.reads: A POST that queries rather than writes — UV's grid, the change logs, the distance and price quotes. Marked so it is not counted as an unverified write.
legend.dependsOn: What must already have happened for this chunk to run. kind=session: a sign-in. kind=data: another chunk captured a variable this one needs, with `alternatives` when more than one chunk can produce it. kind=seeded: the fixture supplies it; no chunk does.
legend.provides: Flow variables this chunk captures for later chunks.
legend.edges: Narrative order — which chunk a tester reaches next. `dependsOn` is the harder constraint: what must run first. The two differ, e.g. audit follows invoice.details in the story but only needs {orderId} and {jobId}.

variables.jobId: Captured at legs.add.submit — a leg is a job in the monolith.
variables.shipperId: From the shipper under test; used by the EDI config page.
variables.driverId: From the driver row in carrier.admin.

nodes.name: Shipments pagination
nodes.note: This page HAS a working pager. The leg-management shipments table (legs.rows) renders none and strands anything past row 25 — same data, same API, two renderers. A direct comparison is the cleanest evidence for that bug.

nodes.name: No quotes message
nodes.selector: div:has-text("This Shipper Does not have any quotes")

nodes.name: Valid until
nodes.note: An expired quote should not be bookable. Worth a case that books one past its date.

api.note: A quote of 0 usually means no lane rate matched — compare against pricing.lanes for the same lane before filing it as a pricing bug.
The read-back expects a 404 — that is the point. A 200 here means the delete only hid the row.
The quoted amount must carry onto the booked shipment. Assert the price, not just that a shipment appeared.

nodes.name: Queue count badge
nodes.note: Must drop by one after a dismiss. The same badge-vs-action check as the carrier pending tasks tabs.

nodes.name: Why it triggered
nodes.note: The explanation the ops team acts on. If it disagrees with the rule's conditions, that is the bug.

api.note: Re-evaluating a fixed shipment should close the exception. If it stays open, the rule and the data disagree.
Undismiss is the inverse route — round-trip it and confirm the queue badge returns.
A dry run — says how many shipments the rule would open without creating anything. Always check this before saving a rule on staging; a broad rule opens thousands.
Read the conditions back — the rule builder serialises a nested condition tree, and that is where a saved rule quietly loses a clause.
The tiles and the workbench KPI cards read the same metrics endpoint. If they disagree, one of them is filtering client-side.

chunks.name: Pricing engine — lane rates, accessorial rates, FSC, tariffs
chunks.note: Everything here feeds the quote and the invoice. A rate change that does not reach q.get or ar.generate is the failure mode worth chasing.

api.note: A bulk rate upload rewrites pricing for every lane in the file. Only ever against a seeded shipper.

nodes.name: Reversible
nodes.note: Reversible means the rate applies in both directions. A reversible rate that only prices one way is a classic miss.

api.note: Then run quotes.q.get on the same lane. A saved rate that does not change the quote is the bug this chunk exists to find.
Unconfirmed rates do not price. Email confirmation is /api/rates/user/lanes/emailConfirm.

nodes.name: Auto-apply
nodes.note: Auto-apply puts the charge on the shipment without anyone requesting it — pairs with acc.drawer.autoApply on the request side.

api.note: Standard rates are the fallback for every customer without a specific rate — a wrong value here moves money everywhere.
A dry run of the step matrix. Check the boundary rows — the min and the first step are where rounding goes wrong.
Then re-rate an order (order.billing) and confirm the fuel line moved. FSC changes are applied by a rerate, not retroactively.

nodes.name: Default
nodes.note: Only one tariff per type should be default. Two defaults is a data bug that prices unpredictably.

api.note: Rates within a tariff are /api/1/tariffRates. Usage across shippers is /api/2/tariffs/usage — check that before editing a live tariff.
